summary: Woodside packs roughly 5,200 people into 11.5 square miles, which works out to about 450 residents per square mile — a density more typical of rural ranchland than the heart of Silicon Valley, yet it sits barely a fifteen-minute drive from Sand Hill Road's venture-capital corridor. The town drapes across the eastern slopes of the Santa Cruz Mountains, threaded with redwood-shaded trails in Wunderlich County Park and Huddart County Park, where evening walks wind through second-growth forest rather than sidewalks — because most roads here have no sidewalks at all. That semi-rural character is the product of deliberate large-lot zoning and equestrian culture; horse crossings on road signs are not decorative. The affordability math is stark even by Peninsula standards: median home values exceed $2 million against a median household income above $250,000, yielding a price-to-income ratio around 8:1, meaning even top-quintile earners face serious leverage to buy. Almost no commercial district exists — a single general store and a handful of restaurants constitute the retail footprint — so groceries, dining variety, and everyday errands pull you toward Redwood City or Palo Alto. Average highs hover near 67°F year-round with nearly nine hours of daily sunshine, producing a mild, dry-summer Mediterranean climate where fog fingers through the ridgeline but rarely lingers in town. Woodside is essentially a residential preserve embedded in one of the world's most expensive job markets, offering forest silence and open sky at a cost that the data makes unmistakably clear.
